message.content:
# Progress Note

**Client:** Roger
**Session:** 1 – Intake
**Presenting Concerns:** Anxiety, Depression

---

## Progress

Roger presented for his initial intake session today and reported that he is not feeling the greatest. He has been having a tough time focusing and noted that when his focus feels off, a lot of other things feel off as well. His anxiety score was 2 and his depression score was 3, both within a manageable range. He identified that the lack of focus is the most distressing aspect of his current experience. Roger is currently staying at the Turning Point shelter and is collecting disability benefits for a Traumatic Brain Injury. We discussed his history of substance use, and he expressed no current desire to use because it causes too many problems. Is the connection between his TBI and his current focus difficulties something he is already aware of? Has he experienced similar episodes of reduced focus in the past? Are there other factors he feels are contributing to his current state?

## Intervention

The session focused on building rapport and gathering comprehensive history. We explored the relationship between his TBI and his current cognitive and emotional challenges. Standardized screening tools were administered to assess his current levels of anxiety and depression. Psychoeducation regarding the impact of TBI on attention and mood was provided. How would Roger describe his typical daily routine at the shelter? What are his primary goals for treatment at this time?

## Response

Roger was engaged and appeared willing to participate in the session. He verbalized that he is motivated to work on his focus and overall well-being. He demonstrated insight into the relationship between his TBI and his current symptoms. Roger indicated that he is willing to continue working with us and will return for a follow-up session. Does he feel comfortable with the direction of our work today? Would he be open to incorporating cognitive exercises into future sessions?
